summary: Open-source platform to trace, evaluate and monitor LLM apps and agents, and to track, register and deploy machine learning models.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: MLflow is an open-source AI engineering platform for agents, LLMs and ML models. For LLM apps it offers tracing (observability), evaluation, prompt management and optimization, and an AI gateway. For classic ML it offers experiment tracking, model evaluation, a model registry and deployment to Docker, Kubernetes, Azure ML, SageMaker and more.
sixtySeconds.problem: Shipping AI to production needs a way to see what your app did, measure quality and manage models over time. MLflow covers that lifecycle in one vendor-neutral tool.
whoFor: Teams building LLM apps and agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a widely used, vendor-neutral platform that works locally or on managed services, with integrations for many agent frameworks and model providers.
requirements: Your model provider's API key for LLM tracing

overview: Start a tracking server with uvx mlflow server, point your code at http://localhost:5000 and turn on autologging, for example mlflow.openai.autolog(). Then run your code and open the UI to see traces and metrics.
A setup wizard can configure tracing for you when run from a Git repo with Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode installed.

It supports Python, TypeScript/JavaScript and Java, plus OpenTelemetry, and can be hosted locally, on-premises or on managed services such as Databricks, SageMaker and Azure ML. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
